desc: Formalize the reduction: per-person constraints on prefix sums P — equality P[L_i]=P[R_i] at endpoints, P[k] >= P[L_i]+1 (forward) / P[k] <= P[L_i]-1 (backward) for interior k; feasibility = no positive-weight cycle in difference-constraint graph.

Characterize component-graph edges: E1 (forward u, endpoint of v strictly inside I_u ⇒ comp(u)→comp(v)), E2 (forward u, backward v, I_u ∩ I_v ≠ ∅ ⇒ comp(u)→comp(v)), E3 (backward u, endpoint of v strictly inside I_u ⇒ comp(v)→comp(u)), plus self-loops; feasibility ⟺ acyclicity of contracted graph (all non-equality edges +1).
Resolve short-witness conjecture: REFUTED — cycles of arbitrary length exist with no short sub-witness, so the cheap pairwise e_i+BIT offline scheme is invalid.

Design the offline algorithm: sqrt-block on L (queries with R ≤ block end answered directly, length ≤ B; rest sorted by R with candidate set = left part L..bnd + right part bnd+1..R), feasibility checked exactly per query via component-graph rebuild + Kahn. Validity follows from downward-closed feasibility (monotone f(L)).
Implement the offline algorithm with optimizations: per-forward `seen` set in E2 segment-tree reporting, early exit on self-loops, DSU + Kahn cycle detection.

Stress-test: brute-force feasibility via Bellman-Ford on raw difference constraints for small random cases vs. the component-graph criterion and the offline algorithm (include long-cycle counterexample cases from the refutation).
Handle edge cases: |S-T|=2 (empty interior, equality only), shared endpoints between persons, nested vs interleaving intervals, 0/1-indexing of prefix array.
Verify performance on worst-case inputs (nested alternating intervals, all-overlapping fwd/bwd families) and add micro-optimizations if needed (iterative segment tree, early termination).
Write final Python solution with fast I/O; verify on samples by reasoning; ensure complexity fits N≤4e5, M,Q≤2e5.
